calls.head: Don’t buy Skinner’s slump against the Stars
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Skinner has been shaky against the Stars, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Skinner starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .901 than to his .832 against the Stars.

calls.head: Where the Stars have the edge: shot quality
calls.body: The Stars are around the middle of the league for shot quality, and the Jets are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Stars’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Jets’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hintz ties it late and wins it in overtime
paras: Wyatt Johnston opened the scoring for the Stars early in the second, with Jason Robertson picking up his 500th NHL point on the goal. Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor scored less than two minutes apart midway through the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. With the goalie pulled and two minutes left, Roope Hintz made it 2-2 for Dallas. Hintz won it with his second goal of the night in overtime.

The Stars carried the play, outshooting the Jets 38-19, but needed overtime to win it. Jake Oettinger made 17 saves for the Stars, and Stuart Skinner kept the Jets in it, stopping 35 of 38. By our Swing measure, Dylan Samberg had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Hintz’s overtime winner in the game.

Neither power play scored: the Stars killed all four Jets power plays, and the Jets killed both of Dallas’. The Stars moved to 6-3-1, third in the Central, while the Jets fell to 4-3-3, slipping to sixth in the Central.
